text: Hello, this is Mark Wildman of Wildman Athletica and today we are going to work on a two-handed half kneeling back position side to side swing. The names on these are long for a reason. The name contains all the information about what the drill is. We don't name it after the name of some Eastern European country. We just put all the words in the name that describe exactly what it is. The side to side swing is a drill you absolutely need to know and work on if you are a heavy club swinger. There are a bunch of ways to lift weights and get strong in all of human history. Barbell is the new one. It's a 100 years old. Originally, it was strong men pulling axles off of trains and lifting them. Kettle bells are thousands of years old. Before they were iron, they were stone. They were Chinese stone padlocks and they were held in Greek. You can find them all the way back to ancient Greece. The thing that you find in every culture everywhere in all of human history is heavy club swinging. You'll find it on temples all over the world. Look at the gods of strength that use big levers or big hammers. You can go down a giant list of them. Probably the most important movement that you can do in heavy club swinging is the two-handed shield cast. This has a bunch of different names in a bunch of different cultures. That's just the name that we use. In order to be good at the shield cast, you need to know the back position swing. We're going to review it and we're going to show it with a couple of different implements because as the lever changes, it becomes easier to see how you're supposed to move. Then we're going to take it and we're going to put it in the half kneeling position. The back position swing starts from the back of the shield cast. When people learn the shield cast, they tend to not drop their thumb down all the way. And the reason that they can't go up in weight or maximize their rotation is because they're not putting their hand in the right spot. When they do that, it looks like this. And they tend never to get to go up in weight. The bottom of the shield cast is the back of the shield cast. And it should be thumb all the way on shirt. This is the part that people mess up. text: Hello, this is Mark Wildman of Wildman Athletica. And today we are going to talk about the most important squat for sports that you can do at home, the kettlebell deck squat. In sports, you fall down all the time. If you practice any type of martial art, if you're a skier, a dirt biker, a mountain biker, an equestrian person, a gymnast, you engage with the ground in some type of roll. Being strong in the roll, learning to keep your body together so you don't slam your skull into the ground, is a pretty big deal. If you are learning a new sport, you are likely to fall down a lot more. The deck squat helps people prepare athletically to engage the ground in a roll and regain their feet. This exercise has at least four preparatory exercises for it. You have the flat back pullover, learning to drive your rib cage down and push your back into the ground. Think of it as a weighted kettlebell crunch where the weight moves, but your body doesn't. Then you do a pullover sit-up, which is a sit-up with load so that you can start to learn the position of the round of the back. Then you have a pullover sit-up press, where your spine goes from being round in flexion to extension. Then you have the squat. We're going to name two versions of the squat that you should work on, the kettlebell goblet squat, which is holding a kettlebell in front of your body with the globe up and the handle down, and a front squat where you hold the kettlebell on one side of your body. If you practice these exercises ahead of time, then you will be more prepared to do this exercise. The version of this exercise we're going to work on today is feet all the way together. There are versions of this with feet apart, but the feet together version solves a lot of problems in the beginning. Your feet should not be turned out for this exercise. Your feet should be pointed straight ahead. Your heels should be generally together. Most important is the toes of your feet should be together. Step all the way up to your kettlebell, toes touch the kettlebell, feet together, no turnout. When people turn out or their feet are wide, they tend to do things like collapse their knees to try to get lower. By putting your feet together and touching, you're going to have to get the movement from where you're supposed to get the movement. You're going to have to bend your knees more, get your tailbone lower, and round your spine. To pick up the kettlebell, point two thumbs towards the sky, get all the way down, pick the kettlebell up, the globe on top, the big round part on top.
